theorems.name: Single-Period Binomial Replication Theorem
theorems.description: In a single-period binomial model with no-arbitrage (d < e^r < u), every contingent claim with payoffs (V_u, V_d) in the up/down states is replicable, and the replicating portfolio cost equals the risk-neutral expected payoff discounted: V_0 = e^{-r} (q V_u + (1-q) V_d) where q = (e^r - d) / (u - d).

metadata.reference: Single-period binomial replication (Cox-Ross-Rubinstein 1979; Shreve I 1.2)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of all three statements: portfolio cost, up-state payoff, down-state payoff. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/Model.lean. Axioms-clean. Multi-period backward induction (binomialPrice) also defined and proved consistent; CRR convergence to BS is upstream.

theorems.name: CRR One-Step Risk-Neutral Martingale Identity
theorems.description: Under CRR parameterization (u_n = e^{σ √Δt}, d_n = e^{-σ √Δt}, Δt = T/n), the risk-neutral up-probability p_n = (e^{rΔt} - d_n)/(u_n - d_n) satisfies p_n · u_n + (1 - p_n) · d_n = e^{rΔt}. The discrete-time discounted asset is a Q-martingale at each step. Exact algebraic identity, not asymptotic.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.CRRConvergence

open MathFin

/-- CRR one-step risk-neutral martingale identity. -/
theorem crr_one_step_martingale_identity {σ T r : ℝ} {n : ℕ}
    (h_du : crrDown σ T n < crrUp σ T n) :
    crrProb r σ T n * crrUp σ T n + (1 - crrProb r σ T n) * crrDown σ T n
      = Real.exp (crrPerStepRate r T n) :=
  MathFin.crr_one_step_martingale h_du

metadata.reference: CRR parameterization, one-step martingale (Hull 21.1, Shreve I 1.2)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Pure algebraic identity following from the definitions of crrUp, crrDown, crrPerStepRate, crrProb. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/CRRConvergence.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: CRR Risk-Neutral Probability Tends to 1/2
theorems.description: Under the CRR parameterization with σ > 0 and T > 0, the risk-neutral up-probability p_n → 1/2 as n → ∞: the per-step Bernoulli increment becomes asymptotically symmetric. This is the analytic step behind the variance limit n · σ² Δt · 4 p_n (1 - p_n) → σ² T in the CRR-to-Black–Scholes correspondence; that limit is not itself stated in this entry.

theorems.name: CRR Variance Limit
theorems.description: Under CRR parameterization, n · σ² · (T/n) · 4 p_n (1 - p_n) → σ² T as n → ∞. The per-step variance of the log-return matches the BS variance to leading order. Direct corollary of crrProb_tendsto_half.

theorems.name: CRR to Black-Scholes: Log-Return Convergence in Distribution
theorems.description: Whenever every step's risk-neutral up-probability is a genuine probability (0 ≤ pₙ ≤ 1 — the non-strict closure of the no-arbitrage condition, which the degenerate n = 0 step satisfies), the law of the n-step CRR risk-neutral log-return — the n-fold convolution of the two-point per-step law — converges weakly to the Black-Scholes normal N((r − σ²/2)T, σ²T). The genuine distributional CLT for the binomial tree, via characteristic functions and Lévy's continuity theorem.

import MathFin.Binomial.CRRCharFun

open MathFin Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- CRR → Black–Scholes, convergence in distribution: under no-arbitrage at every
    step (`0 ≤ pₙ ≤ 1`), the `n`-step CRR risk-neutral log-return law — the `n`-fold
    convolution `crrRowProbMeasure` of the two-point per-step law — converges weakly
    to the Black–Scholes normal `N((r − σ²/2)T, σ²T)`. Re-export of
    `MathFin.crr_tendsto_gaussian_inDistribution` (real derivation in
    `MathFin/Binomial/CRRCharFun.lean`: the per-step charFun is computed exactly,
    its `n`-th power converges to the Gaussian charFun
    (`crr_charFun_pow_tendsto_gaussian`), and Lévy's continuity theorem
    (`ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_of_tendsto_charFun`) upgrades charFun convergence
    to weak convergence, via `charFun_convPow` for the `n`-fold row law). -/
theorem crr_log_return_tendsto_gaussian {r σ T : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hp : ∀ n, 0 ≤ crrProb r σ T n ∧ crrProb r σ T n ≤ 1) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => crrRowProbMeasure r σ T n (hp n).1 (hp n).2) atTop
      (𝓝 (bsLimitProbMeasure r σ T)) :=
  MathFin.crr_tendsto_gaussian_inDistribution hσ hT hp

theorems.name: CRR to Black-Scholes: Binomial Call Price Convergence (Closed Form)
theorems.description: The n-step Cox-Ross-Rubinstein binomial price of a European call converges, as n → ∞, to the Black-Scholes call price S₀Φ(d₁) − Ke^{−rT}Φ(d₂). The classical CRR→BS convergence theorem, completing the discrete-to-continuous pricing correspondence. No-arbitrage is hypothesised at every step with n ≥ 1; n = 0 is excluded because the step degenerates there (Δt = T/0 = 0 forces u = d = 1, where no-arbitrage is impossible), and MathFin.binomialNoArb_crr discharges the hypothesis whenever |r|·√T < σ, so it is satisfiable rather than vacuous.

import MathFin.Binomial.CRRClosedForm

open MathFin Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- **Cox–Ross–Rubinstein → Black–Scholes.** Under no-arbitrage at every step with
    `n ≥ 1`, the
    `n`-step CRR binomial price of a European call converges to the literal
    Black–Scholes call price `S₀·Φ(d₁) − K·e^{−rT}·Φ(d₂)`. Re-export of
    `MathFin.binomialPrice_call_tendsto_bs_closed`
    (`MathFin/Binomial/CRRClosedForm.lean`). The route needs no uniform-integrability
    machinery: the bounded *put* payoff passes to the limit under the distributional
    CLT (`binomialPrice_call_tendsto_bs`), binomial put-call parity lifts the limit
    to the unbounded call, and instantiating `bs_put_formula` on the limiting
    Gaussian lands the closed Φ-form. -/
theorem binomial_call_price_tendsto_black_scholes {r σ T S₀ K : ℝ}
    (hσ : 0 < σ) (hT : 0 < T) (hS₀ : 0 < S₀) (hK : 0 < K)
    (hna : ∀ n, 0 < n → BinomialNoArb (crrUp σ T n) (crrDown σ T n) (crrPerStepRate r T n)) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => binomialPrice (crrUp σ T n) (crrDown σ T n)
        (crrPerStepRate r T n) (fun x => max (x - K) 0) n S₀) atTop
      (𝓝 (S₀ * Phi (bsd1 S₀ K r σ T)
          - K * Real.exp (-(r * T)) * Phi (bsd2 S₀ K r σ T))) :=
  MathFin.binomialPrice_call_tendsto_bs_closed hσ hT hS₀ hK hna

Full formal proof of the headline CRR→BS convergence. Chain: binomialPrice_eq_integral_convPow identifies the binomial price with a discounted expectation against the n-fold convolution row law; the bounded put payoff passes to the limit under weak convergence (the distributional CLT of mf-crr-gaussian-limit); binomial put-call parity (binomialPrice_callPut_parity) lifts the limit to the unbounded call — no uniform-integrability/Vitali machinery needed; exp_neg_mul_integral_put_gaussian_eq instantiates bs_put_formula on the limiting Gaussian N((r−σ²/2)T, σ²T) through the standardisation Z = (· − (r−σ²/2)T)/(σ√T), and Phi_neg lands the literal closed form. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/CRRCharFun.lean + MathFin/Binomial/CRRClosedForm.lean. Axioms-clean. 

2026-08-20 correction: the hypothesis was previously `∀ n, BinomialNoArb …`, quantified over every n including n = 0. That is UNSATISFIABLE — at n = 0, crrStep T 0 = T/0 = 0, so u = d = 1 and BinomialNoArb 1 1 0 demands Real.exp 0 < 1 — which made the theorem vacuously true and its content empty, though the proof never exploited that. The hypothesis is now restricted to 0 < n, which is all the limit consumes (the proof already worked eventually-in-n; only the 0 ≤ p ≤ 1 bound needed n = 0, and that survives via crrProb_zero). MathFin.binomialNoArb_crr proves the restricted hypothesis holds whenever |r|·√T < σ.

theorems.name: American Option ≥ Intrinsic
theorems.description: Along every coin-flip path the discounted intrinsic payoff is dominated by the discounted American value: e^(−rk)·g(S_k(ω)) ≤ e^(−rk)·americanPrice(N−k, S_k(ω)) — the dominance clause of the Snell-envelope characterization at path level, routed through the identification theorem rather than the scalar Bellman max (the American case E = univ of the exercise-set statement discounted_intrinsic_le_bermudanPrice).

import MathFin.Binomial.SnellEnvelope

open MathFin

theorem discounted_intrinsic_le_americanPrice_thm
    (u d r : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (S₀ : ℝ) (N k : ℕ) (ω : ℕ → Bool) :
    Real.exp (-r * k) * g (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d k ω)
      ≤ Real.exp (-r * k) * MathFin.americanPrice u d r g (N - k)
          (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d k ω) :=
  MathFin.discounted_intrinsic_le_bermudanPrice Set.univ u d r g S₀ (N := N) (k := k)
    (Or.inr (Set.mem_univ _)) ω

theorems.name: American Value Process is a Supermartingale (Snell Envelope)
theorems.description: The discounted American value process X_k(ω) = e^(−rk)·americanPrice(N−k, S_k(ω)) on coin-flip paths is a supermartingale under the risk-neutral node average: q·X_{k+1}(up) + (1−q)·X_{k+1}(down) ≤ X_k — the conditional-expectation form E[X_{k+1}|ℱ_k] ≤ X_k on the finite tree, via the identification snellAux = e^(−rk)·americanPrice: the discounted American value is the Snell envelope of the discounted payoff.

import MathFin.Binomial.American
import MathFin.Binomial.SnellEnvelope

open MathFin

theorem discounted_americanPrice_supermartingale_thm
    (u d r : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (S₀ : ℝ) {N k : ℕ} (hk : k < N) (ω : ℕ → Bool) :
    MathFin.crrUpProb u d r * (Real.exp (-r * (k + 1 : ℕ)) *
        MathFin.americanPrice u d r g (N - (k + 1))
          (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d (k + 1) (Function.update ω k true)))
      + (1 - MathFin.crrUpProb u d r) * (Real.exp (-r * (k + 1 : ℕ)) *
        MathFin.americanPrice u d r g (N - (k + 1))
          (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d (k + 1) (Function.update ω k false)))
      ≤ Real.exp (-r * k) * MathFin.americanPrice u d r g (N - k)
          (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d k ω) :=
  MathFin.discounted_bermudanPrice_supermartingale Set.univ u d r g S₀ hk ω

theorems.name: The Binomial Price of a European Claim Is the Cost of Its Hedge
theorems.description: Under no-arbitrage (0 < d < e^r < u) and S0 != 0, for every payoff g and horizon N there is a predictable strategy H (H_{k+1} is strongly measurable for the natural filtration of the first k coin flips, i.e. depends only on them) such that, along every coin-flip path, e^(-rN) g(S_N) = binomialPrice u d r g N S0 + sum_{k<N} H_{k+1} (S~_{k+1} - S~_k) (the martingaleTransform of H against the discounted spot), where S~_k = e^(-rk) S_k is the discounted spot.

import MathFin.Binomial.MartingaleRepresentation

open MeasureTheory MathFin

/-- The binomial price of a European claim is the initial capital of a hedge. -/
theorem binomialPrice_replication' {u d r : ℝ} (h : BinomialNoArb u d r) {S₀ : ℝ}
    (hS₀ : S₀ ≠ 0) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ H : ℕ → (ℕ → Bool) → ℝ, StronglyAdapted flipFiltration (fun n ↦ H (n + 1)) ∧ ∀ ω,
      Real.exp (-(r * N)) * g (spotPath S₀ u d N ω) = binomialPrice u d r g N S₀
        + martingaleTransform H (discountedSpot S₀ u d r) N ω :=

theorems.name: The Binomial Tree's Snell Envelope Is the Library's Snell Envelope
theorems.description: On the coin-flip path space with the law of i.i.d. Bernoulli(q) flips (coinFlipMeasure q) and the natural flip filtration, for a payoff process Z adapted to the flips, the tree's explicit pathwise Snell envelope snell E q Z N k agrees almost surely, at every time k ≤ N, with the library's general Snell envelope snellEnvelope (the backward recursion U_i = max(Z_i, E[U_{i+1} | F_i]) at the exercise times {i | N − i ∈ E}, the bare conditional expectation elsewhere). With q = crrUpProb u d r, the Snell envelope of the discounted payoff e^{−rn} g(S_n) is, almost surely and at every k ≤ N, the discounted Bermudan price e^{−rk} bermudanPrice E (N − k) at the spot S_k. Only the identification is stated: no optimal stopping time is exhibited, and no-arbitrage is not assumed (crrUpProb need not lie in (0, 1)).

import MathFin.Binomial.PathMeasure

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

/-- The tree's pathwise Snell envelope `snell` is, almost surely and at times `k ≤ N`, the
library's `snellEnvelope` for the flip filtration under `coinFlipMeasure q`, exercisable at the
times `i` with `N - i ∈ E`. -/
theorem binomial_snell_ae_eq_snellEnvelope {q : ℝ≥0} (hq : q ≤ 1) {E : Set ℕ}
    {Z : ℕ → (ℕ → Bool) → ℝ} (hZ : ∀ n, PathAdaptedAt n (Z n)) {N k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ N) :
    snell E (q : ℝ) Z N k =ᵐ[coinFlipMeasure q hq]
      snellEnvelope (coinFlipMeasure q hq) flipFiltration {i | N - i ∈ E} Z N k :=
  snell_ae_eq_snellEnvelope hq hZ hk

/-- With `q = crrUpProb u d r`, the Snell envelope of the discounted payoff `e^{-rn} g(Sₙ)` is,
almost surely, the discounted Bermudan price with `N - k` steps to go at the spot `S_k`. -/
theorem binomial_snellEnvelope_discounted_bermudanPrice {q : ℝ≥0} (hq : q ≤ 1) {E : Set ℕ}
    (u d r : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (S₀ : ℝ) (hqcrr : crrUpProb u d r = q) {N k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ N) :
    snellEnvelope (coinFlipMeasure q hq) flipFiltration {i | N - i ∈ E}
        (fun n ω ↦ Real.exp (-r * n) * g (spotPath S₀ u d n ω)) N k
      =ᵐ[coinFlipMeasure q hq] fun ω ↦
        Real.exp (-r * k) * bermudanPrice E u d r g (N - k) (spotPath S₀ u d k ω) :=
  snellEnvelope_discounted_bermudanPrice hq u d r g S₀ hqcrr hk

theorems.name: Willow Tree: the beta identity and moment/marginal preservation under Curran's constraints
theorems.description: The willow tree of Curran prices against a Brownian motion with a discrete-time Markov chain on a fixed node set z_1, ..., z_n carrying a fixed discrete marginal q: the node count per time step is constant, and the lattice widens like sqrt(t) only through the scaling X_k = sqrt(t_k) Z_k. What replaces recombination is a time-inhomogeneous family of transition matrices P_k, each row chosen (in the original construction, by linear programming) to be row stochastic and to match, at every current node z_i, the first two conditional moments of the standardized Brownian pair with correlation beta_k = sqrt(t_k / t_{k+1}): sum_j P_k(i,j) z_j = beta_k z_i and sum_j P_k(i,j) z_j^2 = beta_k^2 z_i^2 + (1 - beta_k^2), together with the marginal constraint sum_i q_i P_k(i,j) = q_j. For t_{k+1} = (1 + alpha_k) t_k the construction's de-correlation coefficient 1 / sqrt(1 + alpha_k) equals sqrt(t_k / t_{k+1}), the correlation of a Brownian motion at two grid times. This entry proves the chain-side core: the beta identity in both forms; that ANY family of transition matrices satisfying the row constraints keeps a chain started at a marginal of mass 1, mean 0 and unit second moment at mass 1, mean 0 and unit second moment at every step (an induction needing neither the marginal constraint nor non-negative entries), so the unstandardized chain X_k = sqrt(t_k) Z_k has second moment t_k at step k; that under the marginal constraint the marginal at every step is the same law q; and the cross moments E[Z_k Z_{k+1}] = beta_k and E[X_k X_{k+1}] = t_k, the Brownian covariance across [t_k, t_{k+1}] that the constraint system encodes. An honest (non-negative, summing-to-one) transition row also forces the coefficient into [-1, 1], and there the standard bivariate normal law with that correlation has unit variances and covariance beta_k. The linear program that finds admissible matrices (feasibility, the objective, entry non-negativity) is not part of the claim, and no statement is made about prices computed on the lattice.

import MathFin.Binomial.WillowTree

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin

/-- The willow `beta` identity: on a grid step widening time by the factor `1 + alpha`,
the de-correlation coefficient `1 / sqrt(1 + alpha)` is `sqrt(t / t')` for
`t' = (1 + alpha) * t` -- the correlation of a Brownian motion at times `t` and `t'`. -/
theorem willow_tree_beta_identity_thm {t t' α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < 1 + α) (ht : 0 < t)
    (ht' : t' = (1 + α) * t) : MathFin.willowBeta α = √(t / t') :=
  MathFin.willowBeta_eq_sqrt_div hα ht ht'

/-- The `beta` identity with `alpha` computed from consecutive grid times as in the
willow construction: `willowBeta ((t (k+1) - t k) / t k) = sqrt(t k / t (k+1))`. -/
theorem willow_tree_beta_identity_grid_thm {t : ℕ → ℝ} (ht0 : ∀ k, 0 < t k) (k : ℕ) :
    MathFin.willowBeta ((t (k + 1) - t k) / t k) = √(t k / t (k + 1)) :=
  MathFin.willowBeta_eq_sqrt_div' ht0 k

/-- Any family of transition matrices satisfying Curran's willow-tree row constraints
(row stochasticity and the conditional first/second moment rows with de-correlation
coefficient `β k`) keeps a chain started at a marginal of mass `1`, mean `0` and unit
second moment at mass `1`, mean `0` and unit second moment at every step `k`; the
standardized cross moment across one step is `β k`, and the unstandardized chain
`X k = sqrt(t k) * Z k` has second moment `t k` at step `k` and Brownian cross moment
`t k` across `[t k, t (k+1)]`. No marginal constraint and no non-negativity of the
entries are needed. -/
theorem willow_tree_moment_matching_thm {n : ℕ} {z : Fin n → ℝ} {q : Fin n → ℝ}
    {β : ℕ → ℝ} {P : ℕ → Fin n → Fin n → ℝ}
    (hP : MathFin.WillowMomentConstraints z β P)
    (hq : ∑ i, q i = 1) (hq0 : ∑ i, q i * z i = 0) (hq2 : ∑ i, q i * z i ^ 2 = 1)
    (t : ℕ → ℝ) (ht : ∀ k, 0 ≤ t k) (ht1 : ∀ k, 0 < t (k + 1))
    (hβ : ∀ k, β k = √(t k / t (k + 1))) (k : ℕ) :
    (∑ j, MathFin.willowMarginal P q k j = 1)
      ∧ (∑ j, MathFin.willowMarginal P q k j * z j = 0)
      ∧ (∑ j, MathFin.willowMarginal P q k j * z j ^ 2 = 1)
      ∧ (∑ i, MathFin.willowMarginal P q k i * z i * ∑ j, P k i j * z j = β k)
      ∧ (∑ j, MathFin.willowMarginal P q k j * (√(t k) * z j) ^ 2 = t k)
      ∧ (∑ i, MathFin.willowMarginal P q k i * (√(t k) * z i)
          * ∑ j, P k i j * (√(t (k + 1)) * z j) = t k) :=
  ⟨MathFin.willowMarginal_mass hP hq k, MathFin.willowMarginal_mean hP hq0 k,
    MathFin.willowMarginal_secondMoment hP hq hq2 k,
    MathFin.willowMarginal_crossMoment hP hq hq2 k,
    MathFin.willowScaled_secondMoment hP hq hq2 t ht k,
    MathFin.willowScaled_crossMoment hP hq hq2 t ht ht1 hβ k⟩

/-- Under the marginal constraint `∑ i, q i * P k i j = q j` the willow marginal is the
same discrete law `q` at every step: the constant node set and constant marginal that
distinguish the willow tree from growing recombining trees. -/
theorem willow_tree_marginal_preservation_thm {n : ℕ} {q : Fin n → ℝ}
    {P : ℕ → Fin n → Fin n → ℝ}
    (hmarg : ∀ (k : ℕ) (j : Fin n), ∑ i, q i * P k i j = q j) (k : ℕ) :
    MathFin.willowMarginal P q k = q :=
  MathFin.willowMarginal_eq hmarg k

/-- An honest (non-negative, summing-to-one) transition row forces the de-correlation
coefficient into `[-1, 1]`, and for such a coefficient the standard bivariate normal law
with that correlation has unit variances and covariance `β k`. -/
theorem willow_tree_feasibility_thm {n : ℕ} {z : Fin n → ℝ} {β : ℕ → ℝ}
    {P : ℕ → Fin n → Fin n → ℝ}
    (hP : MathFin.WillowMomentConstraints z β P) (k : ℕ) (i : Fin n)
    (hrow : ∀ j, 0 ≤ P k i j) :
    β k ^ 2 ≤ 1
      ∧ Var[(Prod.fst : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ); MathFin.bivariateNormalLaw (β k)] = 1
      ∧ Var[(Prod.snd : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ); MathFin.bivariateNormalLaw (β k)] = 1
      ∧ cov[Prod.fst, Prod.snd; MathFin.bivariateNormalLaw (β k)] = β k :=
  MathFin.willowBeta_bivariateNormal_moments hP k i hrow
